items.title_id: Dari Ketergantungan Donor Menuju Pembiayaan Majemuk: Rencana Tindak Lanjut dan Peta Jalan 2030 Tujuh Klinik Layanan HIV Berbasis Komunitas di Indonesia
items.title_en: From Donor Dependence to Mixed Financing: Action Plans and 2030 Roadmaps of Seven Community-Based HIV Clinics in Indonesia
items.abstract_id: Latar belakang: Klinik berbasis komunitas (community-based clinics, CBC) menyediakan layanan HIV, infeksi menular seksual (IMS), dan perawatan, dukungan, dan pengobatan (PDP) yang ramah bagi populasi kunci, tetapi sebagian besar operasionalnya masih dibiayai donor kesehatan global yang akan berakhir pada 2030. Kertas kerja ini mendeskripsikan bagaimana tujuh CBC di Indonesia merencanakan transisi tersebut dan menilai kesenjangan antara target jangka panjang dan tindakan jangka pendek. Metode: Analisis dokumen kualitatif-deskriptif atas tujuh paparan rencana tindak lanjut (RTL) tiga bulan dan peta jalan 2027 hingga 2030 yang disusun tim klinik (pimpinan, staf keuangan, dan perwakilan komunitas) pada lokakarya keberlanjutan November 2026. Data diekstraksi ke matriks terstruktur, dianalisis secara tematik dan deskriptif, dan mutu RTL dinilai dengan empat kriteria turunan prinsip SMART. Seluruh klinik dianonimkan sebagai CBC A sampai G. Hasil: Lima klinik menargetkan porsi donor 0 hingga 10% pada 2030 dan dua lainnya 15 hingga 20%. Kemandirian terutama diharapkan dari pendapatan layanan, filantropi, dan sumber lain (70 hingga 100% di lima klinik), sementara hanya tiga klinik memasukkan Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN) dalam target bauran dana. Enam klinik menargetkan dana daerah 10 hingga 50%, tetapi baru satu yang sudah memperolehnya melalui swakelola tipe III. Dari 24 kegiatan RTL, tidak satu pun menyasar kredensialing JKN, dan hanya dua klinik yang memuat langkah menuju dana daerah. Semua RTL mempunyai penanggung jawab, tetapi dua klinik belum menetapkan waktu dan empat belum merumuskan hasil yang dapat dicek sepenuhnya. Logistik program dan dukungan pendamping sebaya adalah kebutuhan yang paling sering diminta. Kesimpulan: Klinik memiliki visi keberlanjutan yang jelas, tetapi rencananya bertumpu pada pendapatan layanan yang berisiko mengurangi akses populasi kunci, sementara jalur pembiayaan publik (JKN dan kontrak sosial daerah) belum diterjemahkan menjadi langkah konkret. Pendampingan perlu memprioritaskan urutan perizinan, akreditasi, dan kredensialing, uji guardrail akses atas rencana tarif, dan penyelarasan usulan swakelola dengan siklus perencanaan daerah 2028.
items.abstract_en: Background: Community-based clinics (CBCs) provide HIV, sexually transmitted infection (STI), and care, support and treatment services that key populations trust, yet most of their operations are still financed by a global health donor whose support ends in 2030. This working paper describes how seven Indonesian CBCs plan for that transition and assesses the gap between their long-term targets and short-term actions. Methods: A descriptive qualitative document analysis of seven presentations of three-month action plans and 2027 to 2030 roadmaps, prepared by clinic teams (head, finance staff, and community representative) at a sustainability workshop in November 2026. Data were extracted into a structured matrix and analysed thematically and descriptively; action-plan quality was appraised against four criteria derived from SMART principles. All clinics are anonymised as CBC A to G. Results: Five clinics target a donor share of 0 to 10% by 2030 and two target 15 to 20%. Self-reliance is expected mainly from service fees, philanthropy, and other sources (70 to 100% in five clinics), while only three clinics include national health insurance (JKN) in their target funding mix. Six clinics target 10 to 50% from local government budgets, but only one already receives such funds through civil-society contracting (swakelola type III). None of the 24 action-plan activities addresses JKN credentialing, and only two clinics include steps towards local government funding. All plans name a responsible person, but two clinics have not set timelines and four have not fully defined verifiable outputs. Programme commodities and peer support are the most frequently requested forms of assistance. Conclusions: Clinics hold a clear sustainability vision, but their plans rely on service revenue that may reduce access for key populations, while public financing routes (JKN and local social contracting) have not been translated into concrete steps. Support should prioritise the sequence of licensing, accreditation and credentialing, access-guardrail testing of tariff plans, and aligning contracting proposals with the 2028 local planning cycle.
